record.title: Covered clearing-agency recovery and wind-down planning route
record.sub: Recover or resolve a failed institution
kv: Exchange Act clearing-agency framework and SEC Rule 17Ad-22.
A covered SEC-registered clearing agency is within Rule 17Ad-22's applicable recovery and orderly-wind-down requirements.
The Depository Trust Company (registered or chartered); National Securities Clearing Corporation (registered or chartered); Fixed Income Clearing Corporation (registered or chartered)
Covered SEC-registered clearing agencies; Default-management and recovery-plan actors named by an effective clearing-agency rulebook

Identify the registered clearing agency and whether it is covered by the cited provisions. Recover the current recovery/wind-down plan, default rules, liquidity arrangements, and participant obligations. Apply the exact service, product, member, and event rather than an organization-wide label.
A recovery plan is not an observed resolution outcome, a customer guarantee, or a universal default waterfall for broker-dealers, banks, custodians, issuers, or blockchain networks.
The Depository Trust Company: SEC lists DTC as a registered clearing agency.
National Securities Clearing Corporation: SEC lists NSCC as a registered clearing agency.
Fixed Income Clearing Corporation: SEC lists FICC as a registered clearing agency.
